why_angle: The cited rival pages (3dtoolchangers.com/printers, 3dprinteray.com/toolchanger-printers) give only maker swap-time claims and prices. None has a named tester's results on the same model. This page has them: CNC Kitchen's 4-colour cube took under 4 h on the U1 and Prusa XL and about 7 h on the Bambu H2C, and a colour change took about 40 s on the H2C against 10–15 s on a toolchanger. It also has Notebookcheck's Creator 5 Pro waste and prep-time figures and today's prices: U1 $699, Creator 5 Pro $849. The pick, the Snapmaker U1, is not a product we list. Snapmaker isn't in our programs and amzcheck found no U1 on Amazon. Our QIDI and Flashforge Adventurer 5M Pro printers have a single nozzle and win no segment of this question, so the page adds no product of ours.

page.title: Best 3D Printer with a Tool Changer (2026): Measured Print Times, Swap Times and Prices
page.h1: Best 3D printer with a tool changer
page.desc: Five 3D printers with tool changers compared on measured multicolor print times, time per color change, build volume, chamber and today's US price. The Snapmaker U1 leads at $699.
page.answer: Short answer. The best 3D printer with a tool changer for most buyers is the Snapmaker U1 ($699), which swaps four complete toolheads. In CNC Kitchen's same 4-color test, the U1 and Prusa XL tool changers printed in under 4 h; the Bambu H2C, which swaps only hotends, took about 7 h.

cells.test: 4-color cube in under 4 h; prime tower a bit heavier than the XL's (CNC Kitchen). 10–12 s per color change (stlDenise3D)

cells.chamber: Enclosed, active heating up to 65 °C, HEPA + carbon filter (Flashforge)

Same 4-color cube in under 4 h (CNC Kitchen, tested on the original XL)

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Same 4-color cube: about 7 h on the H2C against under 4 h on the U1 and XL, so 7 − 4 = at least 3 h longer on the H2C (CNC Kitchen).
  • Per color change: about 40 s on the H2C against 10–15 s on a toolchanger, or 25–30 s more each time. Over 100 changes that adds 100 × 25–30 s = 42–50 min.
  • U1 swap time: Snapmaker states 5 s as a typical lab result. stlDenise3D timed 10–12 s per color change including the prime. Prusa's figure for INDX is about 12 s, measured from the last extrusion on one tool to the first extrusion on the next. Measured the same way, 10–12 s against about 12 s, the two swap at about the same speed.
  • Waste per change: the U1 made 4.4 g of prime tower over 90 swaps, 4.4 ÷ 90 ≈ 0.049 g each (stlDenise3D). The tuned Creator 5 Pro made 8 g over more than 700 changes, 8 ÷ 700 = under 0.012 g each (Notebookcheck). Prusa states 0.013 g for INDX.
  • Enclosure step-up: Creator 5 Pro $849 − U1 $699 = $150 for an enclosed frame and a chamber heated to 65 °C. Flashforge's open-frame Creator 5 costs $699, the same as the U1.
  • Build volume: the XL+ prints 360³ mm = 46.7 L and the U1 270³ mm = 19.7 L. That is 46.7 ÷ 19.7 ≈ 2.4× the volume for $3,899 − $699 = $3,200 more.
  • Spare toolhead: a complete U1 toolhead with hotend costs $64.99 at Snapmaker's store.

Measured on the same print

CNC Kitchen (Stefan Hermann, 2025-11-18) printed one 28 g, 4-color test cube on the Bambu Lab H2C, the Snapmaker U1 and a Prusa XL toolchanger. In Purge Saving mode the H2C took about 7 hours and built a 23 g prime tower. Standard purge mode was about 10% slower and made a tower about 50% heavier. The U1 and the XL each finished in under 4 hours. Their towers were "more or less comparable", with the U1 "wasting a bit more".

The gap comes from what gets swapped. On the U1, XL+ and Creator 5 Pro, every filament stays loaded in its own complete toolhead, so a change is a pickup and a short prime. The H2C swaps only the hotend and still feeds filament from its AMS. CNC Kitchen measured about 40 s per change including purge, against 10–15 s on a toolchanger, even though the mechanical nozzle swap alone takes under 15 s.

Full-toolhead changers still waste some filament. Parked heads stay hot, so they ooze. Prusa's knowledge base says that with ooze prevention off, every XL extruder stays at print temperature for the whole print, and it sets a minimum prime of 15 mm³ (PLA) to 35 mm³ (other materials) per tool on the wipe tower. INDX tools have no heater of their own: the head heats each nozzle by induction when it picks it up. Prusa says this removes the prime tower and uses 13 mg per change.

Notebookcheck (Silvio Werner) found the Creator 5 Pro needs tuning before it gets there. On factory settings a 16 g Benchy produced 36 g of waste, which tuning cut to 8 g. Preparation before a print using all four filaments took 28 minutes, and about 10 minutes on later prints with the same bed and material.

Not recommended

Avoid the Bambu Lab H2C if you are buying it as a tool changer for faster multicolor prints. It swaps hotends, not toolheads. On the same cube it took about 7 h against under 4 h for the U1, and its Combo costs $2,299 against $699 for the U1. It makes sense when you need its 350 °C hotends and 65 °C chamber more than you need speed.
